member.name: T:Intersect.Client.Core.XraySilhouetteTextureCache
member.summary:
Builds and caches "x-ray" copies of entity/paperdoll textures where each pixel's ALPHA is remapped by TWO factors, both aimed at making the character read as BEHIND cover rather than pasted on top: 1. BRIGHTNESS — darker pixels stay more opaque (dark gear/hair stay visible; a dark hair staying opaque is exactly what keeps the bald scalp from showing through it), while bright pixels (skin, light cloth) go see-through so the cover shows through them. 2. VERTICAL POSITION — the LOWER part of the body becomes more transparent than the upper part (a smooth bottom-to-top gradient within each sprite cell). This mimics being occluded from below: your legs/feet hide behind the trunk/wall while your head peeks out — a strong "I'm behind something" depth cue.
Same approach as : the remap is a per-pixel CPU pass done once per source texture and cached, so the hot draw path swaps in the prebuilt texture. The source pixel's own alpha (feathered edges, transparency) is preserved as a multiplier so edges stay smooth and fully-transparent pixels stay fully transparent.

member.name: M:Intersect.Client.Entities.Entity.AdvanceMovementOffset(System.Single)
member.summary: Advances the walk-offset animation toward 0 on each axis INDEPENDENTLY of facing. The offsets themselves already encode the step's travel direction (they are seeded as "draw me back where I came from", so each axis simply glides to 0 and clamps there) — facing is only sprite-row presentation. DO NOT re-couple this to DirectionFacing: a step can travel a direction the sprite is not facing (the settle-to-grid squaring scoot, and a remote glide whose facing-restore packet lands mid-step). The old facing-switch clamped any offset that disagreed with facing straight to 0, which rendered such steps as quarter-tile TELEPORTS (playtest 2026-07-17). Behaviour is bit-identical for ordinary movement, where the offset signs and facing always agree; it also correctly drains BOTH axes when the remote handler's offset accumulation leaves a residual on the off axis (the old code force-zeroed the perpendicular axis instead).

member.name: P:Intersect.Client.Entities.Player.IsAttackFollowThroughAfterKill
member.summary:
True while the current swing is a post-kill FOLLOW-THROUGH: the victim died, so the swing finishing on screen is pure animation with no living opponent. While set, movement INTENT (keys or a click-move path) is allowed to interrupt the swing exactly the way deliberate mid-combat movement always could — see the attack gate in HandleInput. Cleared whenever a new swing starts.
WHY a flag and not an AttackTimer adjustment: the swing animation's progress is DERIVED from AttackTimer (timeInAttack = CalculateAttackTime() - (AttackTimer - now)), so ANY mutation of AttackTimer mid-swing teleports the animation forward and visibly truncates the killing blow — the exact regression a previous fix caused (playtest 2026-07-16) and the exact reason the 2026-07-01 fix forbids snapping it. The flag leaves the timer (and therefore the animation) completely untouched unless the PLAYER chooses to move.

member.name: M:Intersect.Client.Entities.Player.ExecuteSubTileStep(Intersect.Enums.Direction,System.Guid,System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Applies one validated quarter-tile step: position, walk-offset animation, move packet, and step pacing. This is the SINGLE mutation point for sub-tile steps — both real input () and the auto-settle glide () go through here so the server always sees ordinary, individually-validated move packets and stays lock-step with the client. When is true (settle steps), the character does NOT turn toward the step direction — a settle is a squaring-up scoot, not a walk — and the server's Dir (which MoveSubTile sets from the move) is immediately corrected with a direction packet so remote clients never render a facing flip.

member.name: F:Intersect.Client.Entities.Player._aligningForMelee
member.summary: A square-up-on-engage micro click-move to the player's own tile centre is in progress (issued by the auto-attack in-range branch so melee reads front-to-front against tile-centred mobs). While set: the in-range branch must not clear the click target (that's the alignment walk itself), swings hold, and the click-move destination marker is hidden (a crystal on your own feet is noise). Cleared by the bookkeeping check in Update the moment the click target ends for ANY reason (arrival, watchdog give-up, cancel, input override).

member.name: F:Intersect.Client.Entities.Player._settleSuspendedUntilNextInput
member.summary: The finish-the-step system is suspended: a forward finish was blocked (rule 2) or the server sent a position correction (rule 3 — see ). While set, no automatic steps run and the settle-before-swing gate in stays open, so combat behaves exactly as it did before this system existed (resting a quarter-tile off-centre is the graceful degraded state). Cleared ONLY by a real player-input step — automatic movement must never re-arm itself.

member.name: M:Intersect.Client.Entities.Player.CanAutoSettleNow
member.summary: Whether the finish-the-step glide is allowed to run right now. Deliberately LIVE-COMPUTED (no stored "is settling" flag) so the settle-before-swing gate in can never go stale and block attacks: if this is false, swings proceed exactly as they did before this system existed. Casting matters most here — a finish step is a real move, and real moves cancel casts (MovementCancelsCast), so finishing must wait out any cast.

member.name: M:Intersect.Client.Entities.Player.TrySettleSubTileToTileCenter
member.summary:
FINISH-THE-STEP (tile-to-tile combat alignment, final design 2026-07-17): sub-tile movement lets the player STOP between tile centres, but every combat rule (adjacency, cardinal facing, mob chase) speaks whole tiles — a fractional resting position makes melee look like it connects across a visible gap. When movement input goes idle off-centre, the character keeps walking FORWARD — the direction already being walked — until the next tile centre: the standard grid-game "commit to the tile transition" rule (facing unchanged, walk cycle just continues, a released tap completes a clean tile).
THE THREE HARD RULES, each one bought with a failed playtest — do not relax them: 1. FORWARD ONLY. Never a backward or sideways correction step: any motion that isn't a continuation of the player's own walk reads as "the game moved me" (backward scoots and perpendicular slides both failed playtest). 2. ONE-SHOT. If the forward step is blocked (wall, or the mob itself on the next tile), GIVE UP where we stand (`_settleSuspendedUntilNextInput`) — resting a quarter-tile off is fine; combat gates open and behave exactly as before this system existed. 3. CANCEL ON SERVER CORRECTION. An `EntityPositionPacket` for the local player calls — the server disagreed (usually a mob contesting the tile), and retrying is how the endless client/server snap loop happened: client-initiated automatic movement ALWAYS loses races against moving entities, because a human stops pressing but automatic retries don't. Only real player input re-arms the system.
Steps go through the normal validated per-step move path (), so zero server/packet changes. Guards mirror ProcessDirectionalInput's: no finishing while casting (a move would cancel the cast), during click-move (it owns movement and already ends on tile centres), mid-step, dead, or in dialogs.

member.name: M:Intersect.Client.Entities.Player.SuspendAutoSettleUntilNextInput
member.summary: Rule 3 of the finish-the-step system: the server sent this client a position correction (EntityPositionPacket), meaning our view of the world disagreed with authority — typically a mob moving into the tile a finish step was entering. Automatic movement must NEVER retry after that (endless correction loop, playtest 2026-07-17); only real player input re-arms it.

member.summary: Marker tiles the in-game tile renderer never draws (they only drive shader effects: procedural waterfalls, water shore foam, water reflections). member.name: M:Intersect.Client.Maps.MapInstance.IsWaterfallMarkerTile(Intersect.Framework.Core.GameObjects.Maps.Tile)
member.summary: Waterfall marker tiles (waterfall_start etc.) drive the procedural waterfall shader — in-game they render as a big animated waterfall. Preview renderers (minimap/world map) can't run the shader, so they draw these tiles as flat water-blue fill instead of skipping them (skipping left visible holes where waterfalls exist in-game).

member.summary: Computes a hash of which adjacent grid maps are currently loaded. Used to detect when a neighboring map finishes loading so the water tile cache can refresh its boundary shore masks/depths.

member.name: M:Intersect.Client.Maps.MapInstance.RefreshWaterSurfaceTileCacheForLayer(System.String)
member.summary: Recomputes shore masks and depth levels for water tiles that sit on this map's edges. The cache is built when a map first loads, but neighboring maps may not be loaded yet, so boundary tiles can be cached with wrong shore/depth values. Refreshing once the neighbor is loaded removes the visible seam where connected water continues across maps.
